header.title: How to Clean Corroded Electrical Wires
header.description: This guide provides step-by-step instructions on how to safely clean corroded electrical wires, restoring their conductivity and preventing potential hazards. It covers safety precautions, accessing the wires, and using appropriate cleaning techniques.

steps.description: Prioritize safety by disconnecting power, verifying no electricity, and wearing protective gear when working with electrical wires.
actions: Turn off the circuit breaker at the main panel
Use the current tester to make sure there is no power coming through

steps.description: Remove the faceplate or cover to access the electrical wires within the outlet or electrical box.
actions: Use screwdriver to remove the faceplate over the electrical outlet
Remove the cover to the electrical box
Remove the plastic covering to gain access to the electrical wires
Determine if the electrical wires are corroded by their discoloration
Detach the wires from the contact points
Work one wire at a time
steps.part: faceplate, electrical outlet, electrical box, plastic covering, screws, electrical wires, contact points

steps.description: This step details cleaning electrical wires and connectors of corrosive material using a wire brush and a baking soda solution.
actions: Use the wire brush over the electrical wires.
Scrub the electrical wire and the wire connected with it using a toothbrush dipped in a baking soda and warm water mixture.
Repeat scrubbing until the wire and connector do not produce fizzing.
Reattach the wires to their terminals using new connectors.
